note: The declared registry of quantity names. `subject: {kind: quantity}` resolves against this, and so does numbers[].name. Sibling to observables.json, not a merge with it: that file registers what two agents can PRODUCE and COMPARE, and its entries carry an estimator, a window and a producible_by because comparability is what it exists for. Most named numbers here are produced by nobody and compared with nothing -- a coverslip thickness, a pixel size -- and giving them an estimator to make them fit would be inventing registry structure so a subject resolves, which is the move this repository refused three times on 2026-09-19. Every observable is a quantity; not every quantity is an observable.
why_this_exists: Until 2026-09-19 `quantity` was the one subject kind with no registry, and kb_entry.schema.json said so in its own description -- 'a de facto registry rather than a declared one'. A census that day found 55 distinct numbers[].name across 124 uses with nothing checking any of them, and the collisions were already there: bead_diameter in the simulation against tracer_diameter in the microscope, for one quantity the bridge exists to compare. No two names carried different units, so the store was still coherent and this was the cheap moment.
growth: One entry when a question needs one, the same rule observables.json uses and for the same reason: an unused entry is a definition nobody has tested against data. This file starts with the ids already used as `subject: {kind: quantity}` and defensible from entries on disk, not with all 55 names in use.
rules: A name states the QUANTITY, and never its subject or its locus. This is rule one because both violations were already on disk when the file was written. `tracer_particle_density` puts the subject in the string -- and when check 44 refused the subject field on those entries the claim did not disappear, it moved into the name where nothing checks it. `ambient_temperature` puts the locus in the string, which `at` now carries. `na_mrd70040` does both. A name that asserts its own subject is a subject nothing can refuse.

One name, one quantity, across every card and the store. This is check 36's rule for `symbol` applied to names. What it buys is that the bridge comparing two values can ask whether they are the same quantity by id rather than by string equality on whatever each side happened to call it.

A unit is part of the identity, not an annotation. Two entries writing one name with different units are two quantities, and the registry names the canonical one. No collision of that kind existed on 2026-09-19, which is why the registry can be written from observed usage rather than imposed on it.
Being registered here says a name is well defined. It does not say a value exists, is measured, or is good -- those are the entry's business and its grade's.

Plan parameters are quantities too and follow the same rules, but they are marked, because the bridge only has to reconcile names across agents for the physical ones. Nobody compares one agent's box_margin_factor with another's.

open_collisions.where: bead_diameter in simulation_agent (6 uses), tracer_diameter in microscope_agent (2 uses)
open_collisions.why_it_matters: One physical quantity under two words, held by the two agents whose values the bridge exists to put side by side. observables.json warns that two sides agreeing on a word while disagreeing on the estimator is worse than disagreeing openly; here they do not even agree on the word. Unresolved on purpose: which name survives is not this file's call to make unilaterally over two other seats' cards.

open_collisions.where: diffusivity in simulation_agent (6 uses); tracer_diffusivity is a registered observable; tracer_diffusivity_expected is a derived_quantity entry as of 2026-09-20
open_collisions.why_it_matters: The registered observable and the name the simulation actually writes are different strings. This is the same collision as the one above and it sits on the one observable the bridge is currently threading. A third name joined on 2026-09-20 and it is the dangerous one, because unlike the first two it is NOT the same quantity: `tracer_diffusivity` is what either side MEASURES OR MODELS and `_expected` is what Stokes-Einstein PREDICTS. Two names for one thing is a matching problem; a third name that looks like the other two and is a different claim is a comparison silently made against the wrong operand. The moment it is easiest to slip into a measured or modelled slot is when the bridge thread resumes, which is why the librarian seat raised it before that happened.

open_collisions.where: na in librarian entries (6 uses), the six suffixed forms in microscope_agent
open_collisions.why_it_matters: Rule 1. The lens is the subject and it is in the name; task 009 made part numbers addressable through `identifiers` precisely so it would not have to be.

Rule 1 again, on the locus rather than the subject. `ambient_temperature` is `temperature` read at the room, and `at` exists as of 7320f78 to say that. Listed below as a quantity anyway, because retiring a name in use is the work and not the declaration.

open_collisions.where: working_distance on five objective entries; the min/max pair on objective_mrd77400 alone
open_collisions.why_it_matters:
Not a synonym and not a mistake: a dry or oil lens has one working distance and the 40x water-immersion lens has a RANGE, because its correction collar moves it. So the store is right and a caller still cannot see it. On 2026-09-20 manager-microscope looked for `working_distance` on all six objectives, found five, and reported the sixth as missing -- the value was there under two other names.

What this exposes is bigger than the pair. `kb_query('working_distance')` returns five entries and NO GAP, because five is a real answer. `near_names` only rides on a gap, so a PARTIAL answer offers nothing: five out of six looks complete to anyone who does not already know there are six. The mechanism built to say 'the store calls it something else' fires only when the store says nothing at all.

quantities.definition: The distance at the sample plane that one detector pixel spans. Depends on the objective, the intermediate magnification and the binning, so a value is a claim about one combination of the three and not about the instrument.
quantities.note: The canonical datum for axis A6, which reads pixel size directly; magnification is the derived convenience (plan.md 1137). Backed by twelve calibration entries.

quantities.definition: The ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the material, at a stated wavelength. Dispersive, so a value without a wavelength is not reusable.
quantities.note: Unit is `1`, the name units.json uses. Written `dimensionless` in this file's first commit -- the registry has no such symbol, so rule 3 was broken by the file that states it, one commit after stating it. Eight kb entries carried the other spelling when this was written; measured 0 on 2026-09-20, all eight fixed on 2026-09-19. The sentence outlived the condition by a day and was copied out of here into task 024 as a live constraint, which is the failure this repository keeps naming -- a count read off prose instead of a run, by the seat that had told three others not to.

quantities.definition: Dynamic viscosity: the ratio of shear stress to shear rate in the fluid.
quantities.note: Strongly temperature dependent -- roughly two percent per kelvin for water -- so a value carries its temperature.

quantities.definition: Thermodynamic temperature. Where it was read is a property of the number and belongs in `at`, not in the name.
Temperature of the room air. Registered because it is in use, and flagged: by rule 1 this is `temperature` with `at` naming the room, and the name predates that field.
quantities.note: See open_collisions. Retiring a name already on disk is migration work, not a declaration.

quantities.definition: Thickness of the coverglass between the objective and the sample, as mounted.
Numerical aperture: the refractive index of the medium times the sine of the half-angle of the accepted cone. A property of an objective at a stated immersion.
quantities.note: Which lens is the subject, addressable through identifiers.part_number since task 009. Not a suffix on the name -- see open_collisions.

quantities.definition: Diffusive time: the time a sphere needs to diffuse its own diameter. A derived quantity with a formula rather than a stored value, and it keeps a dimension -- length squared over a diffusivity is a time.
quantities.note: Filed as dimensionless_group with no unit for its first day; that is why kb_entry's kind enum now separates derived_quantity from dimensionless_group.

quantities.definition: Optical power delivered along an illumination path. Where in the path it is measured changes the number, so it belongs in `at`.
quantities.note: The trapping laser's is neither readable nor settable from software, so a value for it is an operator reading of a hand control and not a device readback.

quantities.definition: The Stokes-Einstein PREDICTION of a tracer sphere's translational diffusivity, k_B T / 3 pi eta d. A computed expectation, not an observation: it is what the viscosity, the temperature and the diameter imply, and it is the number a plan compares a measurement against rather than a measurement itself.
quantities.note: Third name in a family of three and the one most likely to be mistaken for the others -- see open_collisions. Held as a derived_quantity with the formula rather than a value, so an improving input improves it; that is also why nothing may recompute it (plan.md 1295).

quantities.definition: The short-time translational self-diffusion coefficient of dilute spherical tracers in the sample: the proportionality between mean squared displacement and lag time in the free regime. What either side MEASURES OR MODELS, as distinct from what Stokes-Einstein predicts.
quantities.note: Registered here on 2026-09-20 because check 60 enforces section 7's inclusion, not because a new question arrived: the name was already blessed at the harder cost, as a registered observable with an estimator and a window. The canonical unit is the first of the two the observable admits (um^2/s, m^2/s) -- a quantity names one unit and an observable may admit several, which is why check 60 compares the ids and not the entries. Second name of the three in open_collisions and the one the bridge currently threads; `tracer_diffusivity_expected` is a different claim and not a synonym.

quantities.definition: The per-axis standard deviation of a trapped particle's in-plane position about the trap centre, over a declared record length. A width, measured without assuming the trap is harmonic.
quantities.note: THE NAME OVERSTATES WHAT THE QUANTITY IS, and it is registered under it anyway. The observable reports a scalar -- sigma -- while the full histogram stays with the raw data, so the registered quantity is a width and the name says distribution. Not renamed here: capabilities/*.json and the bridge resolve answerability against this id, and which name survives is not this file's call to make unilaterally over two other seats' cards -- the same refusal open_collisions records for bead_diameter against tracer_diameter. Rule 1 is not violated (no subject, no locus in the string), so nothing refuses it; this note is the record that it was seen rather than missed. Canonical unit um, of the um and nm the observable admits.

quantities.definition: The detected signal rate a single tracer delivers, under the illumination and detector stated with it. It is a property of dye, lot, illumination and camera TOGETHER, not of the particle, which is why no vendor sheet holds one.
quantities.note: The unit is a rate of detected events per second. Without a camera gain calibration the detector reports counts rather than photons, so a value here is counts per second unless its entry says otherwise -- the gain that would convert them is its own gap. Registered 2026-09-20 because a pre-measurement needs the name; the person settled on 2026-09-19 that for a new sample this closes by imaging the particles alone rather than by asking.

quantities.definition: The decay constant of tracer signal under continuous illumination: the reciprocal of the time over which emission falls by 1/e at a stated illumination. Like tracer_brightness it is a property of the combination and not of the dye alone.
quantities.note: A rate constant, so 1/s. Illumination belongs with it: the same particles bleach faster under more light, and a value carrying no illumination is not transferable. Registered 2026-09-20 alongside tracer_brightness, which the same acquisition produces.

quantities.definition: The rms uncertainty a camera's readout adds to a pixel, in electrons, for ONE readout mode. A value without its mode is not a fact about the camera: the Kinetix 22 offers four and they span an order of magnitude, so naming the quantity without the mode is the same error as naming a working distance without the objective.
quantities.note: Registered 2026-09-20 for 029. The store holds four entries, one per mode, and the task that asked for them said three -- three is the Kinetix 3200 row and the installed camera is a Kinetix 22. The execution seat caught it because the task stated the SCOPE of its source rather than just its numbers, which is the habit two earlier tasks of mine lacked.

quantities.definition: The probability that a photon incident on the sensor produces a counted photoelectron, at a stated wavelength. Dimensionless -- electrons per photon -- and strongly wavelength dependent, so a value without a wavelength is not reusable.
quantities.note: Registered 2026-09-20 for 029. The vendor peak is what the store carries for now, by the person's ruling that the vendor value is the basis until a measurement is taken here. THE CURVE IS NOT AN ENTRY AND THERE IS NO FIELD FOR ONE: 5.3 makes a model's digitisation of a rendered curve an E6 inference that may enter neither a card nor the KB, and the legal shapes are already carried -- a scalar here, points a PERSON read as one entry each with the wavelength pinned, or a vendor numeric table beside the other tables. See the $comment on common.schema.json's `number`.

not_yet_registered.why: Names in use that this file deliberately does not bless yet.
not_yet_registered.pending_015_reason: RELEASED 2026-09-19. The six ids listed here were deferred because they carried the product identification withdrawn by task 015 and four put the subject in the name. Both conditions are gone: 015 was superseded and reversed, and 017 renamed them -- none of the six strings exists in the store any more, they are now abvigen_product_*. The deferral was waiting on a task that was itself withdrawn, which nothing would have noticed: a block whose release condition can no longer occur reads exactly like a block still in force. not_yet_registered.plan_parameters: Roughly half the 55 names in use are one agent's planning knobs -- save_interval_max, box_margin_factor, lag_to_record_ratio, storage_estimate. They follow the same rules and are registered when a question needs the name to mean one thing across a boundary, which for a knob is rarely.
